page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 168.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 42.0 GB per core. It also includes 472 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench scores of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded compression/decompression speeds, such as 34.91 GB/sec in gzip. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by the stress-ng multi-core score of 4441.77 and a weak bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 28.72 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average for cached small blocks at 344.91 GB/sec but drops to weak levels for uncached large blocks, measuring 36.17 GB/sec for reads and 25.69 GB/sec for writes.

Given the high memory density combined with a low vCPU count, this server is designed for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and text processing tasks. The high memory capacity relative to compute resources offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications requiring large in-memory datasets without the licensing or infrastructure costs of higher vCPU counts.
